links.reading: Charles, your questions can help William put a private worry into words. William, you may feel understood before you have explained everything. On the Sunday call, that can make a useful exchange feel easy, but it does not mean you want advice. Behaviour check: Charles asks what William wants from the conversation before offering a solution.

Charles, you can give William steady attention without pressing him to explain every detail. William, you may find it easier to stay in contact when Charles listens without turning the call into a review. The care is available, but you need to use it deliberately. Behaviour check: Charles gives William time to answer, then lets that answer stand.

Charles, you and William take loyalty seriously and tend to honour what you have promised. That steadiness can make the Sunday call dependable, but it can also make a complaint feel like a breach of duty. William, you may keep quiet rather than risk disappointing Charles. Behaviour check: each of you names one small thing you would like changed.

Charles, your unexpected questions can unsettle William's settled view of what he should do. William, you may welcome a fresh possibility, then need to make the choice privately. This can help you loosen an old rule, but Charles cannot choose the new one for him. Behaviour check: Charles asks what William thinks before suggesting a different course.

Charles, you may offer more reassurance or help than William asked for. William, you may appreciate the care and still feel crowded by it. On the Sunday call, one of you can keep expanding the discussion while the other needs it to stop. Behaviour check: Charles asks whether William wants support, advice, or simply a listening ear.

Charles, your confidence in a wider plan can meet William's need to decide for himself. William, you may hear encouragement as pressure when the choice already feels consequential. You can still discuss the future without treating agreement as proof of trust. Behaviour check: Charles asks which part of the plan William wants to consider, and accepts his answer.

Charles, your reliability can help William feel that he does not have to manage every concern alone. William, you may trust care that arrives consistently and without a demand for disclosure. But neither of you benefits if duty replaces an honest answer. Behaviour check: Charles offers one practical kind of help, and William says whether it would help.

Charles, what feels like a clear expression of your choices may not feel warm to William. William, keeping the conversation pleasant may lead you to hide what you would prefer. The difference is workable when neither of you treats politeness as agreement. Behaviour check: William says what he wants plainly, and Charles asks one question before replying.

Charles, you can help William consider options beyond the plan he first expected to follow. William, you may enjoy exploring an idea with him, while keeping the final choice your own. That exchange can be lively without becoming a promise. Behaviour check: you discuss one new possibility, then name clearly whether either of you is committing to it.

Charles, your hopes can soften William's firm sense of what duty requires. William, you may help give those hopes a practical shape, but you could also take on more than you meant to. Keep kindness separate from an assumed obligation. Behaviour check: before agreeing to a plan, William says what he can realistically do.

Charles, you can stay present when William has to make a difficult long-term choice. William, you may value his willingness to take serious concerns seriously. This support works best when Charles does not mistake persistence for permission to direct the decision. Behaviour check: Charles asks what William has already decided, then offers help only if invited.

Charles, your careful questions can sound to William like a decision he has already been asked to accept. William, you may answer politely, then share less. This friction can teach Charles to wait and William to name a limit before the call goes quiet. Behaviour check: Charles lets William finish, then asks what he has not understood.

William, Charles can touch private parts of your life that you may not discuss readily. His concern may feel steady, but you still get to decide what to share. Charles, a quiet answer does not always mean William wants another question. Behaviour check: William names what he is willing to discuss, and Charles stays with that boundary.

Charles, William's presence can reach the private concerns you do not always put into words. You may care deeply about what he is carrying, yet find it hard to know when to ask. William, you may not want every feeling brought into the open. Behaviour check: Charles asks whether William wants to talk, then respects his answer.
